verses.1: Praise the LORD. Praise the LORD from the heavens; praise Him in the highest heights.
verses.2: Praise Him, all His messengers; praise Him, all His armies.
verses.3: Praise Him, sun and moon; praise Him, all the stars that shine.
verses.4: Praise Him, skies of the heavens, and the waters that are above the heavens.
verses.5: Let them praise the name of the LORD, for He spoke and they were made.
verses.6: He set them in place forever; He gave a decree that will not pass away.
verses.7: Praise the LORD from the earth, you sea monsters and all the deeps.
verses.8: Fire and hail, snow and frost, storm winds that do His word.
verses.9: Mountains and all hills, fruit trees and all cedars.
verses.10: Beasts and all cattle, creeping things and birds that fly.
verses.11: Kings of the earth and all peoples, rulers and all judges of the land.
verses.12: Young men and also virgins, old men with the young.
verses.13: Let them praise the name of the LORD, for His name alone is exalted; His glory is over the earth and the heavens.
verses.14: He has raised a horn for His people, praise for all His faithful ones— for the children of Israel, the people who are near to Him. Praise the LORD!

notes:
Notes
- v. 3: "all the stars that shine" — the Hebrew "כּוֹכְבֵי אֽוֹר" is literally "stars of light," but the meaning is clear and natural in English.
- v. 8: "storm winds that do His word" — the Hebrew "רוּחַ סְעָרָה עֹשָׂה דְבָרֽוֹ" is rendered to reflect the poetic parallelism and the meaning that even the storm winds obey His command.
- v. 14: "raised a horn" — the Hebrew "וַיָּרֶם קֶרֶן" is a metaphor for exalting or empowering. "Raised a horn" is a standard idiom for this in poetic texts.
